topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the structure of the cancer lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Biological Foundations and Drivers of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the interplay between endogenous mutation processes, clonal selection, and microenvironmental factors.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine real-world environmental carcinogen exposures, public debates regarding bad luck versus causation, and international epidemiological differences in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious pathogens promote cancer, illustrating the mechanism through the case of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Multi-Stage Carcinogenesis Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, demonstrating how non-mutagenic tumor promoters and chronic inflammation stimulate cell proliferation.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue development and host life stages influence carcinogen vulnerability, providing a comprehensive recap of carcinogenesis mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro testing strategies utilized to detect carcinogen exposures and establish carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Analysis and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by discussing the daily risk-versus-benefit trade-offs associated with carcinogen exposure and summarizing the primary takeaways.
